entries.definition: Acentric means without a center or not having a central point.

entries.definition: Courteous means polite and respectful.
entries.exampleSentence: The courteous waiter made our dinner very pleasant.

entries.decomposition: co+vert 轉→轉到隱藏處→隱秘的
entries.definition: Covert means secret or hidden.
entries.exampleSentence: They had a covert plan to surprise their friend.

entries.decomposition: cred 相信+it→相信能還→信用
entries.definition: Credit means trust or to give recognition.
entries.exampleSentence: Give credit to the team for their hard work.

entries.definition: Decagon is a polygon with ten sides and ten angles.
entries.exampleSentence: A regular decagon has all sides and angles equal.

entries.definition: Decameter is a metric unit of length equal to 10 meters.
entries.exampleSentence: The field is about two decameters wide.

entries.definition: Decelerate means to slow down or reduce speed.
entries.exampleSentence: The car began to decelerate as it approached the red light.

entries.definition: Decigram is a unit of mass equal to 0.1 gram.
entries.exampleSentence: The powder sample weighed only 5 decigrams.

entries.definition: Decimeter is a unit of length equal to 0.1 meter or 10 centimeters.
entries.exampleSentence: The book is about 2 decimeters tall.

entries.definition: Declare means to state something officially or publicly.
entries.exampleSentence: The mayor will declare the festival open tomorrow.

entries.decomposition: de+cline 傾斜→向下傾斜→衰退
entries.definition: Declination means a downward slope or a decline in quality or quantity.
entries.exampleSentence: There has been a gradual declination in the company's profits.

entries.definition: Decode means to convert a coded message into understandable form.
entries.exampleSentence: The spy tried to decode the secret message quickly.

entries.decomposition: deco+rate 適合→使適合美觀→裝飾
entries.definition: Decorate means to make something more beautiful by adding things.
entries.exampleSentence: They decorate the Christmas tree with colorful lights every year.

entries.decomposition: de+duce 引導→從前面引導→推論
entries.definition: Deduce means to reach a conclusion by logical reasoning.
entries.exampleSentence: From the clues, Sherlock Holmes could deduce the criminal's identity.

entries.decomposition: de+fame 名聲→破壞名聲→誹謗
entries.definition: Defame means to damage someone's reputation by false statements.
entries.exampleSentence: Spreading lies to defame a person can lead to legal trouble.

entries.definition: Defeat means to win against someone in a competition or battle.
entries.exampleSentence: The home team defeated their rivals with a score of 4-2.

entries.decomposition: de+fend 打擊→打擊回去→防衛
entries.definition: Defend means to protect from harm or attack.
entries.exampleSentence: The lawyer will defend the client in court next week.

entries.definition: Defer means to postpone or to yield to another's opinion.
entries.exampleSentence: They decided to defer the decision until more information arrives.

entries.decomposition: de+fic 做→做得不夠→缺乏的
entries.definition: Deficient means lacking in some necessary quality or amount.
entries.exampleSentence: The diet was deficient in vitamins, causing health problems.

entries.decomposition: de+fin 界限→劃定界限→定義
entries.definition: Define means to state or explain the meaning of something clearly.
entries.exampleSentence: The dictionary can define difficult words for us.

entries.decomposition: de+fin 界限+ite→有界限的→明確的
entries.definition: Definite means clear, certain, or with exact limits.
entries.exampleSentence: We have a definite plan for the weekend trip.

entries.definition: Deflect means to cause something to change direction.
entries.exampleSentence: The mirror can deflect light in different directions.

entries.decomposition: de+form 形→使形狀改變→變形
entries.definition: Deform means to change the shape of something, usually in a negative way.
entries.exampleSentence: High heat can deform plastic materials.

entries.decomposition: de+gen 產生+erate→產生向壞的方向→退化
entries.definition: Degenerate means to become worse, lower, or less developed.
entries.exampleSentence: Without care, the garden will degenerate into a mess of weeds.

entries.decomposition: de+grade 等級→降低等級→降級
entries.definition: Degrade means to lower in rank, quality, or to treat with disrespect.
entries.exampleSentence: Constant criticism can degrade a person's confidence.

entries.definition: Dehydrate means to remove water from something or to become very dry.
entries.exampleSentence: Running long distances in hot weather can dehydrate you quickly.

entries.decomposition: de+ject 拋→拋下心情→沮喪的
entries.definition: Dejected means feeling sad, depressed, or discouraged.
entries.exampleSentence: He looked dejected after losing the important match.

entries.decomposition: de+liber 自由→自由權衡→深思熟慮
entries.definition: Deliberate means done on purpose or after careful thought.
entries.exampleSentence: The decision was deliberate and not made in haste.

entries.decomposition: de+lic 誘惑→誘人的精緻→精緻的
entries.definition: Delicate means fine, easily damaged, or requiring careful handling.
entries.exampleSentence: The delicate lace dress needs to be washed by hand.

entries.decomposition: de+light 光→使心情明亮→快樂
entries.definition: Delight means great pleasure or joy.
entries.exampleSentence: The children were filled with delight when they saw the fireworks.

entries.decomposition: de+liver 自由→從束縛中釋放→交付
entries.definition: Deliver means to bring or hand over something to someone.
entries.exampleSentence: The pizza delivery man will deliver your order in 30 minutes.

entries.decomposition: de+mand 命令→強烈命令→要求
entries.definition: Demand means to ask for something forcefully or as a right.
entries.exampleSentence: The workers demand higher wages and better conditions.

entries.definition: Deminish means to make or become smaller, fewer, or less important.
entries.exampleSentence: His influence began to deminish after the scandal.

entries.decomposition: demo 人民+cracy 統治→人民統治
entries.definition: Democracy is a system of government in which people vote to choose their leaders.
entries.exampleSentence: Many countries practice democracy by holding free elections.

entries.decomposition: de+molish 堆積→拆掉堆積→拆毀
entries.definition: Demolish means to completely destroy or tear down a building.
entries.exampleSentence: They plan to demolish the old warehouse and build a mall.

entries.decomposition: de+monstr 顯示+ate→顯示出來→展示
entries.definition: Demonstrate means to show clearly how something works or to protest publicly.
entries.exampleSentence: The teacher will demonstrate how to solve the math problem.

entries.decomposition: de+note 標記→標記出來→表示
entries.definition: Denote means to be a sign or symbol of something.
entries.exampleSentence: The color red often denotes danger or stop.

entries.decomposition: de+nounce 宣佈→公開宣佈反對→譴責
entries.definition: Denounce means to publicly criticize or condemn something.
entries.exampleSentence: The leader denounced the violence and called for peace.

entries.definition: Depict means to show or represent something in a picture or words.
entries.exampleSentence: The movie depicts life in a small village during the 1950s.

entries.decomposition: de+plete 充滿→使不充滿→耗盡
entries.definition: Deplete means to use up or reduce the amount of something.
entries.exampleSentence: Overfishing has depleted the fish population in the lake.

entries.definition: Deplore means to feel or express strong disapproval of something.
entries.exampleSentence: Most people deplore cruelty to animals.

entries.definition: Deploy means to position or spread out for effective use.
entries.exampleSentence: The company will deploy new software next month.

entries.definition: Deport means to force a person to leave a country.
entries.exampleSentence: Illegal immigrants may be deported to their home country.

entries.decomposition: de+pose 放→把位置放下去→廢黜
entries.definition: Depose means to remove someone from power or a high position.
entries.exampleSentence: The king was deposed after a long rebellion.

entries.definition: Deposit means to put money in a bank or to leave something somewhere.
entries.exampleSentence: I need to deposit this check into my account today.

entries.definition: Depress means to make someone feel very sad or to push something down.
entries.exampleSentence: Continuous bad news can depress people's spirits.

entries.definition: Deprive means to take something important away from someone.
entries.exampleSentence: Don't deprive yourself of sleep; it's bad for health.

entries.definition: Deride means to mock or express contempt for someone.
entries.exampleSentence: It's cruel to deride people for their mistakes.

entries.decomposition: de+rive 河→從河裡引水→獲得
entries.definition: Derive means to get or receive something from a source.
entries.exampleSentence: Many modern medicines derive from plants.

entries.definition: Descend means to move or go down.
entries.exampleSentence: The plane will descend slowly before landing.

entries.definition: Describe means to give a detailed account of something.
entries.exampleSentence: Please describe the person you saw at the scene.

entries.decomposition: de+sert 分開→分開離開→拋棄
entries.definition: Desert means to abandon someone or a dry sandy area without water.
entries.exampleSentence: Never desert your friends when they are in trouble.

entries.decomposition: de+serve 服務→服務應得→應得
entries.definition: Deserve means to be worthy of something as a result of actions.
entries.exampleSentence: Good students deserve praise and rewards.

entries.decomposition: de+sign 標記→標記出來→設計
entries.definition: Design means to plan or create the look or structure of something.
entries.exampleSentence: The architect will design a modern house for the family.

entries.definition: Gloriously means in a splendid or magnificent way.
entries.exampleSentence: The team won the championship gloriously after years of hard work.

entries.definition: Definitely means without any doubt or certainly.
entries.exampleSentence: I will definitely come to your birthday party tonight.

entries.definition: Greatly means very much or to a large degree.
entries.exampleSentence: We greatly appreciate your help during this difficult time.

entries.definition: Endwise means with the end forward or lengthwise.
entries.exampleSentence: Place the log endwise to fit it through the door.
